sentences.text: It is submitted by learned counsel for the parties that a comprehensive settlement has been arrived at.

In terms of the 12:32:44 IST Reason:
settlement, the proceedings initiated by either party against the other have been agreed to be closed or quashed.
Paragraph 5 of the joint application lists the cases- criminal as well as civil which the parties have agreed to settle.

In this case Final Report No. 428/16 (420,323,341,211,386,506,120B IPC) dated 20.09.2016 has been submitted pending before the Ld. Court of Addl. Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate No. 20, Sanganer Jaipur.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Crime Case No. 4619/18 (420,406,120B, 384 IPC) dated 19.11.2018 before Police Station:
Sanganer Jaipur (East) pending before Sanganer, District Court, Bambala, Jaipur, which has been sought to be transferred by petitioner from Jaipur to Lucknow vide Transfer Petition (Cr.) No. 142 of 2019 pending before this Honble Court listed along with present SLP (Civil) No. 1754 of 2019.

LIST OF CASES FILED AGAINST VAIBHAV MISHRA ARE STATED AS UNDER:
1. Crime Case No. 73/2016 (498A,323,504,506,406 IPC) with Police Station- Mahila Thana, Lucknow pending the Ld. Court of Judicial Magistrate No. 2 Lucknow.
2. Family Case No. 282/2017 filed by Petitioner against the Respondent under Section 12 of Domestic Violence Act, 2005 with Police Station; Cantt, Lucknow pending before Ld. Court of Civil Judge (Junior Division) Room No. 50, Lucknow;
3.

entities.text: Ld. Court of Civil Judge (Junior Division) Room No. 50, Lucknow
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Criminal Misc. Petition No. 8291 of 2017 under Section 484 Cr.
P.C. filed by Respondent for quashing of Family Case No. 282 of 2017 filed by petitioner under Domestic Violence Act, 2005 pending before Lucknow Bench of Honble High Court.
The above criminal cases/complaints and FIRs are hereby quashed.
Likewise Crl.

Miscellaneous Petition NO.
8291/2017 is hereby disposed of and Family Case No. 282/2017, disposed of in terms of this order.
2.
It is also stated by the parties that petitioner Ms. Priyanka would receive 7,00,000/-, in the form of three Demand Drafts (Nos. 48170,48171,48172).
Furthermore, the parties have mutually agreed that their marriage should be dissolved by this Court in the exercise of its power under Article 142 of the Constitution of India.

Priyanka vs Vaibhav Mishra on 17 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196156781/
2 3.
The application is supported by the affidavit of both parties.
The petitioners father Mr. Gori Shankar Giri is present and he has produced his proof of identity (Adhar Card).
A copy of the same has been taken on record.

4. After considering the application and the affidavits filed in support, this Court is satisfied that the parties have entered into a settlement and mutually agreed to dissolve all their disputes amicably.
The application (IA No. 97591/2023)is accordingly allowed.
It is hereby directed that the cases inter se (mentioned above) stand closed/quashed.

5. The marriage between the petitioner Ms. PRIYANKA and the respondent Mr. VAIBHAV MISHRA is hereby declared as dissolved in the exercise of this Courts power under Article 142 of the Constitution of India.
6. The Court places on record its appreciation for the efforts by Mrs. Kiran Bhardwaj, Mediator, who has assisted the parties in settling their disputes.
7. The Registry is directed to draw a decree in terms of the settlement, which is part of the record.
8. The SLP (C ) No. 1754/2019 is disposed of and the connected T.P.(Crl.) No. 142/2019 stands dismissed.
Pending applications, if any, are also disposed of.
(HARSHITA UPPAL) (MATHEW ABRAHAM)
